# Hermes media integration handover

Prepared 2026-09-14 for a follow-up session. This is a handover, not authorization
for additional live changes.

## Goal and remaining work

Hermes on ai-dev should read household playback history and eventually manage
Sonarr, Radarr, and Lidarr through human-approved conversations in **Moshi iOS
and Photon iMessage**. Do not substitute Seerr or an external approval page.

The read-only Plex/Tautulli and Arr phase is deployed and verified. Remaining:

1. Add Jellyfin playback history, including reporting setup if still absent.
2. Design and implement independently verified conversational approvals.
3. Introduce a small set of approved Arr mutations. Deletion comes last.

Recommended order: Jellyfin history, approval-channel feasibility, then narrow
Arr mutations. Direct Portainer Git-source linkage is optional future work,
not a prerequisite for either feature.

## Start the next session here

1. Fetch current main and inspect the working tree before changing anything.
   Do not blindly resume an old feature branch or overwrite this handover.
2. Read this file, `docs/hermes-media.md`, `docs/ai-dev.md`,
   `docs/docker-deployment.md`, and `services/media-broker/README.md`.
3. Confirm the desired next phase with the owner and obtain authorization for
   its live changes, including plugin installation or service restarts.
4. Recheck live versions, channel capabilities, and plugin state. The observations
   below are dated evidence, not a promise that infrastructure is unchanged.
5. Use one Luna implementation writer and a fresh independent reviewer. Discover
   currently available agents/models before dispatch. The parent owns acceptance,
   publication, merges, and live operations. Do not silently switch execution
   protocols when a governed subagent lane fails.

At handover preparation, GitHub confirmed PR #1755 was merged. A subsequent
`git fetch origin main` timed out, so the checkout was not updated to that merge.
The local branch remained `docs/media-broker-image-only-updates` at
`05f2af4b23ea65fabfc2a32e3ee59dcd56ac0237`. This handover was then added locally;
it has not been committed or pushed by this session.

## Completed work and release references

- [PR #1753](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra/pull/1753): read-only broker,
  sanitized Docker observer, host policy, and Hermes integration.
  Merged as `5dc476a3e1338250ba722113811c8cebf645efaa`.
- [PR #1754](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra/pull/1754): Portainer ownership,
  CI coverage, and dependency security patches.
  Merged as `1cd26015002c8f24e8148f227d10e5eb2005136a`.
- [PR #1755](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra/pull/1755): image-only Portainer
  update procedure discovered during the live rollout. **Now merged**, as
  `e8f53c5ec4b381b350cd7b67fa309d2ba45ea1a6`.
- [Production verification comment](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra/pull/1754#issuecomment-5659179639)
  records the patched deployment and Portainer rebuild trap.

There is no outstanding documentation-merge housekeeping item from this phase.

### Last verified production state

- Portainer manages stack `media-broker`, assigned ID **39**, endpoint **3**.
  Container name remains `media-broker-candidate`; the name does not mean it is
  undeployed. Look up IDs again after a restore.
- Stack active, container healthy, MCP **1.28.1** verified inside the container.
- Running image matched the image explicitly built on docker-host from merged
  source `1cd2601`:
  `sha256:2d5193e7d34d5433e02b81d6a6c6d308b768ca6f811f75d85ee8f690498bb13b`.
- Exactly four read-only tools: `arr_library_inventory`, `arr_quality_profiles`,
  `arr_root_folders`, and `tautulli_play_history`.
- Hermes successfully read inventory, profiles, and root folders for all three
  Arr services. A historical Tautulli track query returned one record; only the
  count was reported, not the playback record.
- Unauthenticated requests returned 401; an untrusted Origin returned 403.
  The non-ai-dev laptop could not connect to broker TCP 8765.
- Nonroot/read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, exact
  private bind, and five read-only secret mounts passed runtime checks. No raw
  credential values appeared in the container environment.
- Hermes user gateway remained active with zero restarts. No new gateway restart
  or credential rotation was needed for the patch deployment.
- Expected and running application project sets matched, 15 projects each,
  during ownership handoff. This checks project presence, not ownership of every
  unrelated application in Portainer.
- GitHub reported zero open Dependabot alerts after the security merge. Recheck
  current advisories before the next release.

## Deployment rules that must not be lost

**The broker is Portainer-managed, manually updated, and NOT Git-connected.**
Git remains the canonical source of the application and Compose definition.

Two Portainer 2.45 behaviors were discovered live:

1. Polling belongs to the shared Git source. Creating the broker with
   `AutoUpdate: null` reused source ID 1 and inherited its five-minute polling.
   That scheduler tried an unwanted image pull. Detaching only the broker
   removed its Git workflow, AutoUpdate, and webhook. The other stacks' shared
   five-minute source was left unchanged. Do not reconnect the broker to it or
   disable unrelated stacks' polling as a workaround.
2. A manual update with the canonical `build` block still present rebuilt from
   Portainer's retained old Git context, even with `PullImage: false`. This
   replaced the prepared image with old source. The image-ID acceptance check
   caught it; a healthy container alone would not have.

The working procedure, detailed in `docs/hermes-media.md`, is:

- Check out reviewed source in the root-owned host directory.
- Run host preflight, then explicitly build locked source against
  `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`. Record the built image ID.
- Create an **image-only Portainer deployment copy** by removing only
  `services.media-broker.build` and its `context`/`dockerfile` children.
  Keep the canonical build block in Git and the host checkout.
- Preserve every other runtime/security field and existing nonsecret settings.
  Update only the intended stack through authenticated Portainer operations.
  Set `PullImage: false`, `Prune: false`, with no automatic updates or webhook.
- Require controller completion, health, the exact recorded running image ID,
  the intended installed dependency version, and authenticated application reads.

Do not use the standalone candidate launcher after Portainer takes ownership.
That would create a second deployment controller. Do not assume Portainer runs
preflight, rebuilds the right checkout, or respects per-stack polling isolation.

## Security boundaries and sensitive data

- Backend API keys and the broker bearer remain in host-owned files outside
  Hermes. No raw upstream passthrough or write tools are currently exposed.
- Never print credentials, messages, or individual household playback records.
  Report counts/status only during live verification.
- Preserve Photon/Moshi configuration, unrelated firewall policy, existing
  tokens, and the functioning Docker observer.
- Broker endpoint: `http://docker-host:8765/mcp`. Exact Host
  `docker-host:8765`; exact Origin `http://docker-host:8765`.
- docker-host binds only its verified Tailscale IPv4. The source-pinned
  `DOCKER-USER` exception admits ai-dev through `tailscale0` before the
  unconditional broker-port drop and general established-connection rules.
  ai-dev has corresponding exact endpoint egress. Keep both host firewall and
  Tailscale grant checks. No Traefik/shared 443 or LAN exception was added.
- The broker runs as `65532:65532` with five read-only secret mounts, no Docker
  socket, and no media mounts. The 5 MiB response bound accommodates the observed
  approximately 2.27 MiB Lidarr inventory.
- The Docker observer on port 2375 has no socket. It exposes only bounded,
  sanitized reads through a private socket backend. Its separate non-internal
  frontend is necessary for Docker host-port publication. The backend remains
  internal-only. Preserve this topology and source checksum validation.

## Live locations and access notes

Repository: `/Users/mm/dev/home-infra`.

| Component | Location |
| --- | --- |
| docker-host | `100.96.174.126`; authorized SSH account used was `mm@docker-host`, with passwordless sudo |
| ai-dev | `100.84.159.38`; SSH alias `ai-dev`, management user `michael` |
| Host broker source | `/srv/hermes-media-candidate` |
| Canonical Compose | `services/media-broker/deploy/compose.yml` |
| Host nonsecret settings | `/srv/hermes-media-candidate/services/media-broker/deploy/.env` |
| Source manifest | `/srv/hermes-media-candidate/source-manifest.json` |
| Broker secret directory | `/etc/media-broker/secrets` |
| Observer bootstrap | `/srv/init`; root-owned source and checksum in its restricted `.env` |
| Hermes config | `/home/hermes/.hermes/config.yaml` |
| Hermes environment | `/home/hermes/.hermes/.env` |
| Hermes ownership marker | `/home/hermes/.config/hermes/media-broker.managed` |
| Hermes integration helper | `/home/hermes/.local/bin/manage-hermes-media.py` |
| Hermes Python with YAML | `/home/hermes/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/python` |

Secret files are `broker-token`, `sonarr-api-key`, `radarr-api-key`,
`lidarr-api-key`, and `tautulli-api-key`. Directories are root:65532 mode 0750;
files are root:65532 mode 0640. File-backed Compose secret declarations do not
set host permissions. Do not rotate or copy these into chat.

The ignored local `.envrc` contains `PORTAINER_API` and was mode 0600. If needed,
parse its literal assignment without shell evaluation. Pass the API credential
through protected stdin to remote Python, never command arguments or output.
The local Portainer API is `https://127.0.0.1:9443` on docker-host. Prior operations
used it through SSH. Never dump full stack/container metadata containing env.

Hermes runs a **user** gateway unit, not a root system unit. Its UID was 30033:

```sh
sudo -n -u hermes env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/30033 \
  systemctl --user status hermes-gateway.service
```

Use explicit Bash/Python for ai-dev remote commands; its login shell is fish.
Check status without printing message-bearing journals into the conversation.

Protected rollback/evidence locations on docker-host:

- `/var/lib/hermes-rollout/security-1cd2601`: prior source, old/new image IDs,
  build log, saved controller definition, image-only deployment copy, and
  `runtime-verified.json`.
- `/var/lib/hermes-rollout/observer-31da1267c641`: earlier observer/firewall
  backups and Portainer adoption/detach metadata.
- Old image tag `home-infra/media-broker:rollback-5dc476a` was retained for
  emergency rollback. It contains the old SDK, not the security patch.

## Jellyfin history work

The earlier audit found the Playback Reporting plugin absent. Recheck before
installing anything; the current broker has no Jellyfin adapter.

Plan:

1. Establish installed Jellyfin version, supported reporting-plugin version,
   current activity/playback data, storage, and backup/retention requirements.
2. Obtain approval for plugin installation and any Jellyfin restart. Determine
   exactly what can be queried and whether useful old records already exist.
   Do not promise backfill. Reliable collection may start only at enablement.
3. Select the narrowest usable authentication and keep its credential in a new
   host-managed broker secret, not Hermes or Portainer environment values.
4. Implement a read-only adapter with exact endpoint allow-listing, bounded
   requests/results/date ranges, no redirects or environment proxies, sanitized
   errors, and explicit source identification.
5. Test movies, episodes, music, user attribution, time zones, pagination,
   sessions versus completed plays, missing records, authorization failures, and
   empty results. Distinguish Jellyfin records from Plex/Tautulli records.
6. Review, merge with authorization, preflight/build, and deploy using the
   image-only Portainer procedure. Verify live using counts only.

An empty query does not prove that no playback occurred. Avoid claiming complete
household history until collection and retention coverage are established.

## Conversation-approved Arr mutations

This requires a new authorization boundary, not just enabling native prompts.
Earlier research found Hermes/Moshi/Photon native confirmation mechanisms are
not independently enforced against a compromised or instruction-following
Hermes process with the same UID and access to its files.

Required design:

- Hermes proposes an immutable, exact plan. The plan identifies service, target
  IDs, intended values, relevant previous state, and expected side effects.
- A separately owned service keeps authoritative plan state and validates
  human approval. Hermes must not be able to create approval evidence, edit the
  verifier's state, access its credentials, or invoke an ungated write path.
- Approval arrives inside Moshi or Photon from a verified authorized human,
  bound to the correct conversation and plan. A text string such as "yes",
  supplied or quoted by the agent, is not evidence of approval.
- Bind approvals to plan identity/content, expiration, and one-time consumption.
  Recheck target state immediately before execution. Changed plans or relevant
  state require fresh approval. Handle retries without duplicate side effects.
- Give the executor only explicitly supported typed actions. Keep backend keys
  outside Hermes and avoid generic URL, method, or arbitrary-payload forwarding.
- Maintain a restricted audit trail without leaking credentials or household
  message/playback contents into ordinary logs.

First investigate the actual trusted ingress available in each channel. Verify
sender identity, message provenance, replay protection, and separation from
agent-controlled credentials. Do not assume either channel supplies signed
callbacks or an adequate independent approval API. If neither can provide a
trustworthy path, present that blocker and design choices to the owner rather
than pretending the normal confirmation dialog solves it.

Suggested initial scope, to agree with the owner:

- Add an explicitly identified movie, series, or artist.
- Change monitoring state or an explicitly named quality profile for one target.
- Treat immediate searching/downloading, root-folder changes, moves, rescans,
  and bulk operations as separate side effects requiring explicit scope.
- Exclude deletion and destructive filesystem operations initially.

Tests must cover forged/quoted approvals, agent-originated echoes, wrong sender
or conversation, expired/replayed approvals, plan tampering, stale library
state, concurrency, partial failure, retry/idempotency, and direct bypass of the
verifier. Start with dry-run plans and a tightly bounded live action only after
independent review and owner authorization.

## Code and validation pointers

- Broker: `services/media-broker/src/media_broker/{server,config,adapters}.py`
- Broker tests: `services/media-broker/tests/test_broker.py`
- Deployment guards: `services/media-broker/deploy/{preflight,launch}.sh`
- Packaging/preflight/container tests: `tests/media-broker-*.sh`
- Hermes integration: `ansible/roles/ai-dev/tasks/hermes-media.yaml` and
  `ansible/roles/ai-dev/files/manage-hermes-media.py`
- Focused Ansible checks: `ansible/tests/hermes-media*.sh`
- Inventory: `docker/portainer-stacks.yaml`
- Observer: `docker/init/agent-observer/observer.py`, `docker/init/compose.yml`,
  `tests/agent-observer_test.py`
- CI: `.github/workflows/_quality-gate.yaml` and `docker.yaml`

Use **uv 0.12.5**, not an arbitrary installed uv version, for locked validation.
The accepted lock resolved MCP 1.28.1, pytest 9.0.3, and pytest-asyncio 1.3.0.
The latter was necessary because 1.2.0 excludes pytest 9. All 25 broker tests,
Ruff, packaging/preflight, isolated Docker smoke, and CI passed. Three upstream
warning messages remained. Advisory-specific exploit tests were not added;
transport/task non-use was also inspected independently.

Earlier research and review artifacts are local, not repository files. Relevant
reports live under:

Treat older plans as historical evidence. The Portainer live findings and
merged runbook override any earlier recommendation for ordinary shared Git
polling or uploading the unchanged build-bearing Compose definition.

## Addendum 2026-09-14: Jellyfin history phase deferred by owner decision

The owner selected the deferral option after this session's read-only audit.
No live Jellyfin changes were made: no plugin installation, no restart, no
credential creation, and no broker changes. Repository state at audit time was
clean `main` at `e8f53c5` matching `origin/main` (the PR #1755 merge), with only
this untracked handover file present.

### Verified live state (aggregate facts only)

- Jellyfin `10.11.11`, image digest `sha256:aefb67e6...b35db`, matching the
  compose pin; container healthy.
- Playback Reporting plugin absent, rechecked before any recommendation.
- No structured playback history exists in `jellyfin.db`: only unstructured
  ActivityLog text events (about 3,590 playback start/stop rows since
  2025-05-02) and per-item UserData play states. Any future collection starts
  at enablement; no backfill is possible.
- Broker and Jellyfin share the `proxy` Docker network, so a future adapter
  needs no new reachability work (`http://jellyfin:8096`).

### Why deferred: upstream plugin is broken on this exact server version

- Jellyfin 10.11.9+ removed `IUserManager.Users`, breaking many plugins at
  runtime with `MissingMethodException`.
- Playback Reporting fixed this in v18 (tag commit `e899995`), but v18 was
  never fully released to the stable channel (plugin issue #133, open).
- The stable catalog (verified via the repo.jellyfin.org manifest on
  2026-09-14) offers only v17.0.0.0 (`targetAbi 10.11.0.0`, reported broken on
  10.11.9+ by open issues #128 and #135) and v19.0.0.0 (`targetAbi 12.0.0.0`,
  Jellyfin 12 preview only). Plugin GUID
  `5c534381-91a3-43cb-907a-35aa02eb9d2c`.
- The community workaround is an untrusted third-party DLL zip; rejected.
- Considered and rejected: downgrading Jellyfin to 10.11.8, building history
  from text-only ActivityLog polling, and adding a webhook push path.

### Resume conditions and first steps

Resume when either a stable-channel Playback Reporting release targets the
running 10.11.x line, or the server moves to a Jellyfin 12 release with plugin
v19 available. Re-verify rather than trusting this addendum:

1. Recheck the plugin's catalog entry and the state of issues #128, #133, and
   #135, plus the installed Jellyfin version and digest pin.
2. Re-obtain owner authorization for plugin installation and any restart.
3. Then follow the original plan: dedicated Jellyfin API key in a new
   host-managed broker secret (`/etc/media-broker/secrets`), read-only adapter
   with exact endpoint allow-listing and bounded requests/results, counts-only
   live verification, image-only Portainer deployment.

Session hygiene note: one early ActivityLog query printed event text into the
conversation before the counts-only discipline was applied. No credentials or
tokens were involved. Future live queries against household data must project
aggregate counts only.

# media-broker

Read-only MCP broker for household media services. This repository owns the
application source, its tests, and the published container image. The
production deployment (Portainer stack, host firewall, secret files) is owned
by the [`mich-murphy/home-infra`](https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra)
repository; see its `docs/hermes-media.md` for the deployment runbook.

This project exposes a small MCP server over the official Python SDK's
Streamable HTTP transport. The adapters target Sonarr 4.0.19 (API v3), Radarr
6.3.0 (API v3), Lidarr 3.1.0 (API v1), and Tautulli 2.18.1. It has four tools:

- `arr_library_inventory` (Sonarr, Radarr, or Lidarr; bounded local pagination)
- `arr_quality_profiles`
- `arr_root_folders`
- `tautulli_play_history` (movie, episode, or track; inclusive maximum 31-day range and optional numeric user filter)

There are no write tools, generic upstream requests, approval endpoints, Seerr,
or Jellyfin integrations. Arr APIs return arrays, so inventory pagination is
performed after one bounded response and reports that fact honestly.

## Local run

Create one file for the broker bearer token and one file for each upstream API
key, with restrictive permissions. The environment contains paths only, never
key values:

export LIDARR_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8686

export TAUTULLI_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8181

name: Quality Gate Template

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      check:
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  static:
    name: ${{ inputs.check }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Install Nix
        uses: cachix/install-nix-action@13d8dd58da0234aa297dedd986986ccb8e7f3e24 # v31
      - name: Cache Nix store
        uses: nix-community/cache-nix-action@7df957e333c1e5da7721f60227dbba6d06080569 # v7.0.2
        with:
          # Per-check keys: the gate jobs run in parallel and build different tools,
          # so a single shared key would only ever persist the first job's store.
          primary-key: nix-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.check }}-${{ hashFiles('flake.nix', 'flake.lock') }}
          restore-prefixes-first-match: nix-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.check }}-
          # Trim oversized stores before saving; GitHub evicts least-recently-used
          # caches once the repo exceeds its 10GB total.
          gc-max-store-size-linux: 5G
      - name: Check flake
        if: inputs.check == 'nix'
        run: nix flake check
      - name: Lint workflows
        if: inputs.check == 'actions'
        run: nix shell .#actionlint --command actionlint
      - name: Check Terraform formatting
        if: inputs.check == 'terraform'
        run: nix shell .#terraform-ci --command terraform-ci -chdir=terraform fmt -check -recursive
      - name: Lint Proxmox template scripts
        if: inputs.check == 'terraform'
        run: nix shell .#shellcheck --command shellcheck terraform/scripts/*.sh
      - name: Validate Terraform roots
        if: inputs.check == 'terraform'
        env:
          TF_IN_AUTOMATION: "true"
        run: |
          nix shell .#terraform-ci --command bash -euo pipefail <<'SCRIPT'
          for dir in terraform terraform/network; do
            echo "Validating ${dir}"
            terraform-ci -chdir="${dir}" init -backend=false -input=false -lockfile=readonly
            terraform-ci -chdir="${dir}" validate
          done
          SCRIPT
      - name: Render Compose files
        if: inputs.check == 'docker'
        env:
          ADMIN_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          ADMIN_USERNAME: REDACTED
          AGENT_OBSERVER_SOURCE_SHA256: e522cce75cee8e596b4bec51119582e4c6ce9c0d12668c79ae593c7852399adb
          AGENT_PROXY_BIND: 100.64.0.1
          CF_API_EMAIL: ci@example.invalid
          CF_DNS_API_TOKEN: REDACTED
          COLLABORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          COLLABORA_ADMIN_USERNAME: REDACTED
          COUCHDB_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          DATABASE_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          DB_DATABASE_NAME: immich
          DB_DATA_LOCATION: /tmp/immich-db
          DB_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          DB_USERNAME: immich
          ENCRYPTION_KEY: REDACTED
          MAXMIND_LICENSE_KEY: REDACTED
          MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND: "true"
          MEDIA_BROKER_BIND: 100.64.0.2
          MEDIA_BROKER_BIND_HOST: 0.0.0.0
          MEDIA_BROKER_SECRETS_DIR: /tmp/media-broker-secrets
          NEXTCLOUD_DB_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          NEXTCLOUD_REDIS_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          PLEX_CLAIM: REDACTED
          JELLYPLEX_JELLYFIN_TOKEN: REDACTED
          RADARR_URL: http://radarr:7878
          LIDARR_URL: http://lidarr:8686
          SONARR_URL: http://sonarr:8989
          TAUTULLI_URL: http://tautulli:8181
          JELLYPLEX_PLEX_TOKEN: REDACTED
          TZ: Australia/Melbourne
          UPLOAD_LOCATION: /tmp/immich-upload
        run: |
          nix shell .#shellcheck --command shellcheck \
            scripts/check-portainer-drift.sh \
            tests/docker-hardening.sh \
            tests/media-broker-stack.sh
          nix shell .#docker-compose .#portainer-drift-tools --command bash -euo pipefail <<'SCRIPT'
          scripts/check-portainer-drift.sh --source-only
          # The hardening check renders and validates every Compose file once.
          tests/docker-hardening.sh
          # Docker-free contract checks; the full mode needs a local daemon.
          tests/media-broker-stack.sh --source-only
          SCRIPT
      - name: Check ai-dev maintenance command
        if: inputs.check == 'ansible'
        run: |
          nix shell .#shellcheck --command shellcheck \
            ansible/roles/ai-dev/files/ai-dev-maintenance \
            ansible/roles/ai-dev/files/reload-nftables \
            ansible/tests/ai-dev-maintenance.sh \
            ansible/tests/docker-host-storage.sh
          ansible/tests/ai-dev-maintenance.sh
      - name: Lint Ansible
        if: inputs.check == 'ansible'
        # galaxy install: kewlfft.aur is not bundled with nixpkgs ansible
        run: |
          nix shell .#ansible-lint --command bash -euo pipefail <<'SCRIPT'
          cd ansible
          ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yaml
          # CI cannot decrypt the real vault; syntax-check needs only the file's
          # shape to load the complete play composition.
          printf '%s\n' '---' > group_vars/secrets.yaml

# Image-only stack; never add a build block (docs/hermes-media.md).
# The Renovate digest bump is the deploy trigger Portainer polls for.
services:
  media-broker:
    image: ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main
    container_name: media-broker
    user: "65532:65532"
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    read_only: true
    networks:
      - proxy
    # MEDIA_BROKER_BIND is a Portainer stack variable holding this host's
    # verified Tailscale address. It has no fallback value.
    ports:
      - "${MEDIA_BROKER_BIND:?set MEDIA_BROKER_BIND in Portainer stack variables}:8765:8000"
    environment:
      SONARR_URL: "${SONARR_URL:?set Sonarr URL}"
      RADARR_URL: "${RADARR_URL:?set Radarr URL}"
      LIDARR_URL: "${LIDARR_URL:?set Lidarr URL}"
      TAUTULLI_URL: "${TAUTULLI_URL:?set Tautulli URL}"
      SONARR_API_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/sonarr_api_key
      RADARR_API_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/radarr_api_key
      LIDARR_API_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/lidarr_api_key
      TAUTULLI_API_KEY_FILE: /run/secrets/tautulli_api_key
      MEDIA_BROKER_TOKEN_FILE: /run/secrets/media_broker_token
      MEDIA_BROKER_BIND_HOST: "${MEDIA_BROKER_BIND_HOST:?set 0.0.0.0 only with explicit opt-in}"
      MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND: "${MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND:?set true only with exact allow-lists}"
      # Hermes uses this fixed authority over the Tailscale endpoint.
      MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOWED_HOSTS: docker-host:8765
      MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOWED_ORIGINS: http://docker-host:8765
      # Lidarr's observed inventory is about 2.27 MB; keep a 5 MB hard bound.
      MEDIA_BROKER_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES: "5242880"
    secrets:
      - source: media_broker_token
        target: media_broker_token
        uid: "65532"
        gid: "65532"
        mode: 0440
      - source: sonarr_api_key
        target: sonarr_api_key
        uid: "65532"
        gid: "65532"
        mode: 0440
      - source: radarr_api_key
        target: radarr_api_key
        uid: "65532"
        gid: "65532"
        mode: 0440
      - source: lidarr_api_key
        target: lidarr_api_key
        uid: "65532"
        gid: "65532"
        mode: 0440
      - source: tautulli_api_key
        target: tautulli_api_key
        uid: "65532"
        gid: "65532"
        mode: 0440
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python3", "-c", "import socket; s=socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 8000), 2); s.close()"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

secrets:
  media_broker_token:
    file: "${MEDIA_BROKER_SECRETS_DIR:-/etc/media-broker/secrets}/broker-token"
  sonarr_api_key:
    file: "${MEDIA_BROKER_SECRETS_DIR:-/etc/media-broker/secrets}/sonarr-api-key"
  radarr_api_key:
    file: "${MEDIA_BROKER_SECRETS_DIR:-/etc/media-broker/secrets}/radarr-api-key"
  lidarr_api_key:

  tautulli_api_key:
    file: "${MEDIA_BROKER_SECRETS_DIR:-/etc/media-broker/secrets}/tautulli-api-key"

edits.oldText:
## Deployment rules that must not be lost

**The broker is Portainer-managed, manually updated, and NOT Git-connected.**
Git remains the canonical source of the application and Compose definition.

Two Portainer 2.45 behaviors were discovered live:

1. Polling belongs to the shared Git source. Creating the broker with
   `AutoUpdate: null` reused source ID 1 and inherited its five-minute polling.
   That scheduler tried an unwanted image pull. Detaching only the broker
   removed its Git workflow, AutoUpdate, and webhook. The other stacks' shared
   five-minute source was left unchanged. Do not reconnect the broker to it or
   disable unrelated stacks' polling as a workaround.
2. A manual update with the canonical `build` block still present rebuilt from
   Portainer's retained old Git context, even with `PullImage: false`. This
   replaced the prepared image with old source. The image-ID acceptance check
   caught it; a healthy container alone would not have.

The working procedure, detailed in `docs/hermes-media.md`, is:

- Check out reviewed source in the root-owned host directory.
- Run host preflight, then explicitly build locked source against
  `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`. Record the built image ID.
- Create an **image-only Portainer deployment copy** by removing only
  `services.media-broker.build` and its `context`/`dockerfile` children.
  Keep the canonical build block in Git and the host checkout.
- Preserve every other runtime/security field and existing nonsecret settings.
  Update only the intended stack through authenticated Portainer operations.
  Set `PullImage: false`, `Prune: false`, with no automatic updates or webhook.
- Require controller completion, health, the exact recorded running image ID,
  the intended installed dependency version, and authenticated application reads.

Do not use the standalone candidate launcher after Portainer takes ownership.
That would create a second deployment controller. Do not assume Portainer runs
preflight, rebuilds the right checkout, or respects per-stack polling isolation.

## Repository split completed 2026-09-17

## Deployment pipeline (current)

Merging to media-broker `main` deploys without manual host steps:

1. **Publish**: dedicated-repo CI pushes `:main` plus an immutable
   `:sha-<commit>` tag to GHCR.
2. **Pin**: the Compose reference here is `:main@sha256:<digest>`. Renovate
   updates the digest when `:main` moves and automerges under the existing
   digest-automerge rule. Run Renovate's workflow dispatch to pin a fresh
   release immediately instead of waiting for its cron.
3. **Redeploy**: the digest bump is a commit on home-infra `main`, which is
   what Portainer's Git polling watches.

The digest pin is the deploy trigger: Portainer compares Git commits and
never consults the registry. Rollback is `git revert` of the digest bump, or
an emergency editor update pinning a known `:sha-<commit>` tag.

**Never add a `build:` block to this Compose file.** The two Portainer 2.45
incidents (per-source polling scheduler; rebuild from a retained stale Git
context when a build block exists, even with `PullImage: false`) are
preserved in `docs/hermes-media.md`. The earlier "do not connect this stack
to the shared source" rule is obsolete — the broker is explicitly allowed on
it now — but must be understood as contingent on the image coming from GHCR.

## Conversation-approved Arr mutations

This requires a new authorization boundary, not just enabling native prompts.
Earlier research found Hermes/Moshi/Photon native confirmation mechanisms are
not independently enforced against a compromised or instruction-following
Hermes process with the same UID and access to its files.

Required design:

- Hermes proposes an immutable, exact plan identifying service, target IDs,
  intended values, relevant previous state, and expected side effects.
- A separately owned service keeps authoritative plan state and validates
  human approval. Hermes must not be able to create approval evidence, edit
  the verifier's state, access its credentials, or invoke an ungated write
  path.
- Approval arrives inside Moshi or Photon from a verified authorized human,
  bound to the correct conversation and plan. A text string such as "yes",
  supplied or quoted by the agent, is not evidence of approval.
- Bind approvals to plan identity/content, expiration, and one-time
  consumption. Recheck target state immediately before execution. Changed
  plans or relevant state require fresh approval. Handle retries without
  duplicate side effects.
- Give the executor only explicitly supported typed actions. Keep backend
  keys outside Hermes; avoid generic URL, method, or arbitrary-payload
  forwarding.
- Maintain a restricted audit trail without leaking credentials or household
  message/playback contents into ordinary logs.

First investigate the actual trusted ingress available in each channel:
sender identity, message provenance, replay protection, separation from
agent-controlled credentials. Do not assume either channel supplies signed
callbacks or an adequate independent approval API. If neither can provide a
trustworthy path, present that blocker and design choices to the owner rather
than pretending the normal confirmation dialog solves it.

Suggested initial scope, to agree with the owner: add an explicitly
identified movie/series/artist; change monitoring state or an explicitly
named quality profile for one target. Treat immediate
searching/downloading, root-folder changes, moves, rescans, and bulk
operations as separate side effects requiring explicit scope. Exclude
deletion and destructive filesystem operations initially.

Tests must cover forged/quoted approvals, agent-originated echoes, wrong
sender or conversation, expired/replayed approvals, plan tampering, stale
library state, concurrency, partial failure, retry/idempotency, and direct
bypass of the verifier. Start with dry-run plans and a tightly bounded live
action only after independent review and owner authorization.

# Hermes media-broker ownership and updates

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->

Portainer owns the read-only broker as an **ordinary Git-connected stack**
named `media-broker`, using the same repository source and polling as every
other inventoried stack. The application source and its container image live
in the dedicated [`mich-murphy/media-broker`](https://github.com/mich-murphy/media-broker)
repository; this repository owns only the stack definition at
`docker/media-broker/compose.yml` and the host policy around it.

This describes the target state. Until the one-time migration runbook below
is performed, the live stack is still the earlier manually updated one.

## Deployment pipeline

Merging to `main` in the media-broker repository deploys without manual host
steps, using the same digest-pin trigger every other stack relies on:

1. **Publish**: the media-broker repository's CI runs the source suite and,
   on merge to `main`, pushes the image to GHCR as
   `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main` plus an immutable `:sha-<commit>`
   tag kept for rollback and audit.
2. **Pin**: the Compose reference here is `:main@sha256:<digest>`. Renovate
   (already authenticating to ghcr.io as `mich-murphy` via its hostRules)
   updates the digest whenever `:main` moves and automerges the PR under the
   repository's existing digest-automerge rule. Renovate runs on a cron
   schedule; use its workflow dispatch to pin a fresh release immediately.
3. **Redeploy**: the digest bump is a commit on home-infra `main` — exactly
   the change Portainer's Git polling watches. It redeploys the stack and
   pulls the pinned digest.

The digest pin is the deploy trigger, not a style preference: Portainer's
auto-update compares repository commit hashes and never consults the
registry, so an unpinned moving tag would stay stale until an unrelated
commit happened to land. Portainer's only registry-aware feature is an
inbound registry webhook, which is unusable here (nothing gets through
Tailscale, and GHCR does not offer registry webhooks).

Rollback is `git revert` of the digest-bump commit (Portainer redeploys the
previous digest on the next poll) or an emergency editor update pinning a
known `:sha-<commit>` tag. Do not re-add a `build:` block to the Compose
file; Portainer must never build this image (see history below).

## Why this stack was previously manual

Complete the migration of the media-broker from `home-infra` to the dedicated `mich-murphy/media-broker` repo: clean up home-infra post-extraction, then get the broker running in Portainer as a Git-connected stack with working auto-updates (Renovate digest-pin → automerge → Portainer redeploy). Longer-term handover items (Jellyfin history, conversational approvals, Arr mutations) remain open but not active.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Live operations require explicit owner authorization; owner owns acceptance, merges, live operations
- Never dump stack metadata containing environment variables/secrets; use counts-only verification
- Host firewall access is via SSH as `mich-murphy@docker-host` for reads; `sudo mm@docker-host` for changes; never run remote sudo
- GitHub API: use gh/api curl, treat counts/dates/URLs as authoritative; no browser automation
- User prefers lean repo hygiene: remove unneeded tests/files, avoid duplicated test coverage (chose trim option B over keep/delete)
- Handover doc itself instructs: don't overwrite it, don't blindly resume old branches

## Progress
### Done
- [x] home-infra pulled; `origin/main` advanced `b95af7f` → `3861304`
- [x] media-broker repo (`/Users/mm/dev/media-broker`) pulled; PRs #1 (production-hardening) and #2 (public-repo-prep) merged; repo now PUBLIC; main at `1514f74`; CI green; merged local branches cleaned
- [x] Rebased `broker-extraction` onto main (one modify/delete conflict on `services/media-broker/pyproject.toml`, resolved by keeping deletion); force-pushed; PR #1769 became MERGEABLE with all 5 checks passing (actions, ansible, docker, nix, terraform)
- [x] Cleanup audit: wired orphaned `ansible/tests/hermes-media.sh` + `hermes-media-firewall.sh` into ansible quality gate (shellcheck + execution; firewall test runs via `nix shell .#ansible-lint`); fixed exec bit 644→755 after CI Permission denied failure; added `.DS_Store` to .gitignore; removed stale local `.ruff_cache`
- [x] Trimmed `tests/media-broker-stack.sh` (option B): removed `cap_drop ALL`, `no-new-privileges` asserts (covered by `tests/docker-hardening.sh`) and direct drift-script call (own gate step); kept build-block ban, image-ref pattern, fail-closed binds, DOCKER-USER policy, negative fixture
- [x] **PR #1769 merged by user**; local main at `f6c7837`; merged branches pruned (`broker-extraction` content-identical to main)
- [x] User made GHCR package public; verified: anonymous token works, `:main` manifest → HTTP 200, tags include `main`, `sha-1514f74426b2`, etc.

### In Progress
- [ ] Portainer stack migration (runbook steps 3–7 from `docs/hermes-media.md`): pending user's answer on whether assistant drives it via SSH + Portainer API or user does it in UI

### Blocked
- Jellyfin playback history: deferred; Playback Reporting plugin broken on Jellyfin 10.11.x (stable catalog only v17 broken / v19 needs Jellyfin 12 preview)

## Key Decisions
- **Rebase (not merge) broker-extraction onto main**: user's explicit choice; verified tip equivalence via diff
- **Wire orphaned tests into CI rather than delete**: they cover live config (`manage-hermes-media.py`, nftables media rule) and pass
- **Keep `tests/media-broker-stack.sh` trimmed (option B)**: unique coverage is build-block ban (Portainer incident guard), image-ref pattern (deploy trigger), fail-closed binds, firewall policy — rest duplicated elsewhere
- **Make GHCR package public**: simplest path; skips Portainer registry credentials AND Renovate `read:packages` token requirement (web-UI-only operation, no REST API support)
- **Kept branches**: `feat/hermes-portainer-promotion` (2 unique patch-IDs vs main, squash-merge artifacts — user told to delete manually if unneeded), `cleanup/trim-infra-tests` (linked worktree), `feat/k8s-apps-tools-auth` (local work)

## Next Steps
1. Get user's answer: assistant drives migration via SSH + Portainer API (`.envrc` has `PORTAINER_API`, tunnel to `https://127.0.0.1:9443`), or user does it in Portainer UI
2. Delete old Portainer stack `media-broker` (ID 39, endpoint 3) — brief downtime; container `media-broker-candidate` goes away; DO NOT delete `/etc/media-broker/secrets`
3. Recreate as Git stack: repo `https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra.git`, ref `refs/heads/main`, compose path `docker/media-broker/compose.yml`, AutoUpdate polling enabled; env values copied from `/srv/hermes-media-candidate/services/media-broker/deploy/.env` on docker-host (root-owned): four upstream URLs, `MEDIA_BROKER_BIND=100.96.174.126`, `MEDIA_BROKER_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0`, `MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND=true`; `MEDIA_BROKER_SECRETS_DIR` optional (defaults `/etc/media-broker/secrets`)
4. Verify: container `media-broker` healthy; running digest = current `:main`; authenticated reads for all 4 tools; 401 unauthenticated; non-ai-dev client firewalled; NO Hermes gateway restart needed; keep existing ACL/token
5. Watch for first Renovate digest-pin PR on home-infra → automerge → Portainer redeploy within ~5 min = end-to-end pipeline proof
6. Open housekeeping decision: untracked `docs/hermes-media-handover.md` has stale code pointers (broker source now in media-broker repo) — refresh and commit, or keep local

## Critical Context
- Repos: `/Users/mm/dev/home-infra` (on main, `f6c7837`), `/Users/mm/dev/media-broker` (on main, `1514f74`; remote `git@github.com:mich-murphy/media-broker.git`)
- Broker exposes exactly 4 read-only tools: `arr_library_inventory`, `arr_quality_profiles`, `arr_root_folders`, `tautulli_play_history`; no write/approval/Jellyfin/Seerr endpoints
- Publish pipeline: media-broker `ci.yaml` publishes `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main` + `:sha-<12>` per main merge; deploy trigger is home-infra Renovate digest bump (`config:best-practices` pinDigests + final automerge rule for digest/pinDigest/patch), NOT Portainer registry polling
- Emergency rollback materials: `/var/lib/hermes-rollout/security-1cd2601` on docker-host (old stack def + verified images + `.env` backup); `home-infra/media-broker:rollback-5dc476a` image retained on host
- Portainer quirks (from preserved incident history in `docs/hermes-media.md`): v2.45 polls per Git source not per stack; can rebuild from retained Git context if a `build:` block exists — hence never re-add one
- Handover's remaining phases: conversational approvals (Moshi iOS / Photon iMessage trusted-ingress feasibility first), then narrow Arr mutations (deletion last)
- Handover warns live facts are dated; at handover time: Portainer 2.45.0, ai-dev 100.85.66.70, docker-host 100.96.174.126, Hermes gateway on ai-dev:4100 runs as user `hermes`

## Original Request
The user reported "done, broker is starting now" — they had completed the Portainer UI recreation of the `media-broker` stack themselves (per a pre-existing runbook). The implicit task for the assistant: perform the runbook's step-5 verification of the redeployed broker, then watch for the expected Renovate digest-pin PR.

## Early Progress
- The assistant decided running read-only verification is appropriate (status/counts only, no env dumps, no credentials printed, per a handover's "live verification discipline").
- Planned verification steps:
  1. Resolve the anonymous GHCR digest for `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main`.
  2. SSH to `docker-host` (user `mm`, passwordless sudo; host also reachable via Tailscale IP `100.96.174.126`) to check: container named exactly `media-broker` (old `candidate` container gone), healthy status, running image RepoDigest matches registry digest.
  3. Unauthenticated `curl` to `http://100.96.174.126:8765/mcp` → expect HTTP 401.
  4. From the user's Mac (non-ai-dev laptop): `nc -z 100.96.174.126 8765` should fail (DOCKER-USER firewall only allows ai-dev).
  5. Authenticated MCP `initialize` handshake via python over SSH on docker-host (token read from `/etc/media-broker/secrets/broker-token` inside python — never printed, never in argv; requires `Host: docker-host:8765` and allowed-Origin headers per `MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOWED_HOSTS`).
- First tool call succeeded: resolved registry digest for `:main` = `sha256:91fee67d2e3ff83179be0765cffc5af404f267573a3eed7990615e302ed9dd45`.

## Context for Suffix
- Next actions: SSH verification script on `docker-host` comparing the running container's RepoDigest against `sha256:91fee67d...`, confirming health/status and absence of the `candidate` container, then the 401 check, the laptop firewall-denial check, and the authenticated MCP initialize (report only HTTP status, server name, negotiated protocol version, tool names — never household data or credentials).
- The broker listens on the Tailscale IP `100.96.174.126` host port `8765` (maps to container port 8000); broker env/secrets/ACLs unchanged from previously verified deployment.
- Remaining runbook item after verification: ask the user (or observe) a quick Hermes conversation check (e.g., Sonarr inventory count via Hermes agent on ai-dev), and watch for the Renovate digest-pin PR (Renovate runs via `.github/workflows/renovate.yaml` cron).

content.text:
- Stack and Compose project: `media-broker`; container: `media-broker`
- Compose path: `docker/media-broker/compose.yml` (image-only)
- Image: `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main@sha256:...` (Renovate-pinned;
  unpinned only briefly before Renovate's first pin after introduction)
- Registry credentials: the package is private, so Portainer needs a `ghcr.io`
  registry entry. This is manual UI state, not established by this repository;
  add it in migration step 3 and audit it after a restore
- Update policy: shared Git polling; Renovate digest bumps are the trigger

Portainer supplies the interpolated `SONARR_URL`, `RADARR_URL`, `LIDARR_URL`,
`TAUTULLI_URL`, `MEDIA_BROKER_BIND`, `MEDIA_BROKER_BIND_HOST`,
`MEDIA_BROKER_ALLOW_PUBLIC_BIND`, and optional `MEDIA_BROKER_SECRETS_DIR`.
These values are URLs, nonsecret bind settings, and a host directory path.
Compose fixes the secret-file paths and the Host/Origin allow-lists. Never put
a backend API key or broker bearer value in Portainer's stack variables,
Compose environment, Git, or command arguments.

The fixed endpoint is `http://docker-host:8765/mcp`, with Host
`docker-host:8765` and Origin `http://docker-host:8765`. The host port binds
only the docker-host Tailscale IPv4. It is not exposed through Traefik, a LAN
exception, or shared port 443. The broker runs nonroot with a read-only
filesystem and has no Docker socket or media mounts.

## Host-side controls that remain

- The five files in `/etc/media-broker/secrets` (`broker-token`,
  `sonarr-api-key`, `radarr-api-key`, `lidarr-api-key`, `tautulli-api-key`)
  stay host-managed: directories `root:65532` mode `0750`, files
  `root:65532` mode `0640`. File-backed Compose secrets do not enforce their
  declared ownership or mode, so verify these after any host rebuild.
  Future ai-dev Ansible runs require the existing bearer as
  `hermes_media_broker_token` through protected variables.
- The host firewall admits TCP 8765 only from ai-dev's exact Tailscale
  address through `tailscale0`; the `docker-host` role defines and asserts
  the `DOCKER-USER` rules on every run.
- The broker uses a 5 MiB upstream-response bound for the observed 2.27 MiB
  Lidarr inventory.

## One-time migration runbook

Performed once, from the old manual stack to the Git stack. Steps 3 onward
assume the pull request introducing `docker/media-broker/compose.yml` has
already merged, because Portainer resolves that path from `refs/heads/main`.

1. Merge that pull request to `main` and confirm the Compose file resolves
   there.
2. Ensure the first image exists: the media-broker repository's `publish`
   job must have run on `main` so GHCR serves
   `ghcr.io/mich-murphy/media-broker:main`.
3. In Portainer, add `ghcr.io` registry credentials with pull access to the
   private package (classic PAT with `read:packages`). Skip this step if the
   package is made public.
4. Delete the existing `media-broker` stack (brief downtime; the old
   container name `media-broker-candidate` goes away with it). Do not delete
   host secret files.
5. Recreate the stack from Git: repository
   `https://github.com/mich-murphy/home-infra.git`, reference
   `refs/heads/main`, compose path `docker/media-broker/compose.yml`, the
   same nonsecret environment values as before, AutoUpdate polling enabled on
   the shared source. No relative-path volumes are needed for this stack.
6. Wait for the container to become healthy, then verify: the running image
   is the current `:main` build; authenticated reads from Hermes succeed for
   all four tools; unauthenticated requests are rejected; a different client
   is denied. Retain the existing ACL and token. No Hermes gateway restart
   is required.
7. Confirm Renovate opens and automerges the initial digest-pin PR for the
   image, and that Portainer redeploys on it. From then on, every
   media-broker merge becomes a Renovate digest bump → automerge → Portainer
   redeploy. If Renovate cannot resolve the digest, its token lacks
   `read:packages` for the private package — fix the token before relying on
   the pipeline.

This remains a read-only integration. Conversation-approved writes and
Jellyfin playback reporting are not enabled. Host controls are operational
policy, not a security boundary against root administrators.
